Implements the per-request `metrics` (`--enable-per-request-metrics`) roadmap item in #44280. Speculative-decoding acceptance stats remain a separate checklist item.

## Summary

- Accept `--enable-per-request-metrics` in the Rust frontend and reject it alongside `--disable-log-stats`.
- Carry the engine's queue, schedule, first-token, and last-token timestamps through decoded text and chat output.
- Return Python-compatible timing fields in non-streaming `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/completions` responses. For streaming, attach them to the final usage chunk when `stream_options.include_usage` is enabled.
- Serialize unavailable timing fields as `null` in non-streaming responses and omit them from streaming usage chunks, matching Python's recursive `exclude_none=True` behavior.

## Scope

Speculative-decoding acceptance metrics are intentionally not included in this PR. `GenerateOutput` already carries terminal `spec_decode_metrics`, but mapping those values into the OpenAI `PerRequestMetrics.speculative_decoding` response field is separate follow-up work.

## Duplicate-work check

- #44280 tracks this Rust frontend gap.
- #36383 is a Python frontend draft. #42198 concerns response headers. #56914 concerns reasoning/content token metrics in Python. None adds this Rust frontend response-body implementation.
- Rechecked open PRs and #44280 comments before branch upload; no Rust timing-metrics duplicate was found.

## Tests

- `cargo fmt --all` — passed.
- `cargo test -p vllm-llm -p vllm-text -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server -p vllm-cmd --quiet -- --test-threads=1` — passed (1,019 tests passed, 1 ignored). An earlier parallel rerun intermittently missed an unrelated `preprocess_audio_secs` snapshot key in `vllm-chat`; that test passed in isolation and in the serial suite.
- `cargo check --workspace --tests` — passed after the review updates.
- `cargo test -p vllm-chat --lib` — passed (351 tests).
- `cargo test -p vllm-llm --lib` — passed (14 tests).
- Focused `vllm-server` metric, completion, and chat streaming tests — passed.
- `cargo clippy -p vllm-llm -p vllm-text -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` — passed after the review updates.
- Ruff, pre-commit, and Python collection for `test_chat_completion.py` — passed. The existing Rust frontend Buildkite step runs this file and now covers non-streaming metrics and the final streaming usage chunk.
- Live serving check on NVIDIA A100X with cached `HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct`, `--enable-per-request-metrics`, `--enforce-eager`, and `max_tokens=8`: non-streaming chat and completions both returned five numeric timing fields; streaming chat and completions each returned metrics in exactly one chunk, the final usage chunk. All four requests completed with eight generated tokens. This checks response behavior, not model accuracy or performance.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to implement and test this change. The human submitter reviewed and tested the original implementation and will review the latest reviewer-driven update before merge.

detail.body:
Implements the per-request `metrics` (`--enable-per-request-metrics`) roadmap item in #44280. Speculative-decoding acceptance stats remain a separate checklist item.

## Summary

- Accept `--enable-per-request-metrics` in the Rust frontend and reject it alongside `--disable-log-stats`.
- Carry the engine's queue, schedule, first-token, and last-token timestamps through decoded text and chat output.
- Return Python-compatible timing fields in non-streaming `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/completions` responses. For streaming, attach them to the final usage chunk when `stream_options.include_usage` is enabled.
- Serialize unavailable timing fields as `null` in non-streaming responses and omit them from streaming usage chunks, matching Python's recursive `exclude_none=True` behavior.

## Scope

Speculative-decoding acceptance metrics are intentionally not included in this PR. `GenerateOutput` already carries terminal `spec_decode_metrics`, but mapping those values into the OpenAI `PerRequestMetrics.speculative_decoding` response field is separate follow-up work.

## Duplicate-work check

- #44280 tracks this Rust frontend gap.
- #36383 is a Python frontend draft. #42198 concerns response headers. #56914 concerns reasoning/content token metrics in Python. None adds this Rust frontend response-body implementation.
- Rechecked open PRs and #44280 comments before branch upload; no Rust timing-metrics duplicate was found.

- Ruff, pre-commit, and Python collection for `test_chat_completion.py` — passed. The existing Rust frontend Buildkite step runs this file and now covers non-streaming metrics and the final streaming usage chunk.
